output.brief:
The cancellation rise is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from a broken Quillbook invoice connection. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. Those failures were logged as warnings, so the health panel never showed them. Churn among Quillbook-connected accounts rose from about 2% to about 6% a month, whether or not they were on the price lock. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%) at every seat size, and that includes the accounts that got the full increase. The earlier link between dollar increase and churn came from bigger accounts being the ones using Quillbook. Among Quillbook accounts, 34% of those with failures had left, against 8% of those without. Slow support responses probably made it worse, but that is not proven as a separate cause.

What to do next:
- Make the Quillbook fix (move to the new interface, 3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority.
- Contact all Quillbook accounts, including those who have left, to correct their invoices.
- Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, because it stops duplicates reaching customers' books.
- Don't roll back the price on 1 September (about $220k a month).
- Don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild. Review its log first.
- Make connector warnings visible on the health panel.
